Playbook.name: Windows — Suspicious Print Spooler SPL File Created - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: An .spl file was created in System32\spool\PRINTERS by a process other than the legitimate spooler binaries - associated with PrintNightmare-class spooler exploitation. Triage question: spooler exploitation for SYSTEM code execution, or a benign print job?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Print spooler exploitation (PrintNightmare and variants) yields SYSTEM code execution and is a known privilege-escalation/RCE vector.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

Signal.Name: Suspicious SPL file
Signal.Details: .spl in spool\PRINTERS by a non-spooler process.

Input.name: $hostname
Input.description: Host where the SPL file was created.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the SPL file creation is spooler exploitation or a benign print job.

Step.name: The SPL file and creating process
Step.Purpose: A non-spooler process writing to the PRINTERS directory is the exploitation signature.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-* | WHERE event.code == "11" AND host.name == "$hostname" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | WHERE file.path RLIKE "(?i).*.*system32.*spool.*printers.*.*" AND file.extension RLIKE "(?i)spl" | KEEP @timestamp, process.name, process.executable, file.path, user.name | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: spoolsv.exe/printfilterpipelinesvc writing .spl is normal. cmd/powershell/rundll32/an unknown process writing there is exploitation. Note the writing process.

Step.name: Did the host then show SYSTEM code execution
Step.Purpose: A new service/process as SYSTEM shortly after the SPL write indicates successful exploitation.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-*,logs-system.system-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND event.code IN ("7045","4697","4688") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 1 hours | KEEP @timestamp, event.code, winlog.event_data.ServiceName, process.name | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 10
Step.AnalystNotes: A new service/SYSTEM process right after the SPL write confirms exploitation - escalate to IR.

Node.Condition: An .spl file written to PRINTERS by a non-spooler process, especially followed by SYSTEM code execution.
A .spl created by the legitimate spooler during a normal print job.
SPL creation by an unclear process.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-SPL-CREATE, INV-02-SPL-EXEC to the case.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm normal printing; close as false_positive.
Isolate the host; open IR; ensure spooler patches are applied.
Disable the spooler where not needed; hunt estate-wide.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A misconfigured print component writing unexpectedly.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
